[[Category:Special function]][[Category:Activation function]]
[[File:Sigmoid function.png|thumbnail|]]
The '''sigmoid function''', also known as the '''logistic function''', is a bounded, differentiable, and real-valued [[special function]], commonly used as an [[activation function]] in [[artificial neural network (ANN)|artificial neural networks (ANN)]].

It is the inverse of the [[logit function]].

== Definition ==

$$
\sigma:\mathbb{R}\to(0,1)\\
\sigma(x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}}.
$$

== Properties ==

=== Limits ===

The sigmoid is strictly increasing, with limits

$$
\lim_{x\to-\infty}\sigma(x)=0,
\qquad
\lim_{x\to+\infty}\sigma(x)=1.
$$

=== Symmetry ===

$$
\sigma(-x)=1-\sigma(x).
$$

=== Derivative ===

$$
\dot{\sigma}(x)=\sigma(x)\bigl(1-\sigma(x)\bigr).
$$

== Generalised form (Richard's curve) ==

$$
\sigma(z):\mathbb{R} \to (0,L)
\sigma(z)=\frac{L}{1+e^{-k(z-z_0)}},
\qquad L>0,\ k>0,\ z_0\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

The standard sigmoid function is then the special case $L=1$, $k=1$, and $z_0=0$.

=== Properties of the generalised form ===

=== Limit ===

$$
\begin{cases}
\lim_{z\to-\infty}\sigma(z)=0,\\
\lim_{z\to+\infty}\sigma(z)=L.
\end{cases}
$$

=== Symmetry according to $z=z_0$ ===

$$
\sigma(2z_0-z)=L-\sigma(z).
$$

=== Derivative ===

$$
\dot{\sigma}(z)
=
k\,\sigma(z)\left(1-\frac{\sigma(z)}{L}\right).
$$
